rationale: No race telemetry exists yet (iteration 0), so this is a conservative first draft built from the contract. Geometry: five line sensors spread across the front of the body (x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, y = 0.04 m ahead of the axle) with 12 mm footprints, so the line is seen by at least one or two sensors across the 25 mm tape at normal offsets. A 0.12 m wheel track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.12 m body width and 0.8 kg mass keep the yaw inertia moderate and the off-track limit comfortable. Controller: weights are scaled to the sensor spacing (about 50 times the x position), so the signal runs roughly -1.5 to +1.5. kp = 2 gives a proportional turn of about 1 for a 1 cm offset, which is a firm but not twitchy correction. kd = 0.2 damps the swing across the line at speed. ki = 0 avoids integral windup on the bends. base_speed = 1.6 (about 80 percent of full PWM) is chosen to reach the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in under 3 s while leaving room to hold the line. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot turns back toward the side it last saw the tape. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some risk on the slalom where the proportional gain may be too weak for tight alternation. The next race should show whether the speed or the gain is the limiting factor.
